1.title: Character
levels: No ones: you build willpower consciously, and practising assertiveness pays off.
One 1: a gentle character; you give way to others easily.
Two 1s: a balanced character. You can stand your ground without forcing it.
Three: a strong will and a need to lead; watch out for stubbornness.
Four or more: a very strong will, which easily turns into stubbornness and a wish to control others. Flexibility is worth practising.

2.title: Energy
levels: No twos: you draw energy from other people and from rest, so look after your recovery.
One 2: enough energy for everyday life, but easy to lose when there is too much going on.
Two 2s: a good reserve of energy and sensitivity to your surroundings.
Three: a lot of energy, which needs an outlet so that it does not turn into nervousness.
Four or more: enormous energy that can tip into oversensitivity; exercise and rest are needed.

3.title: Curiosity
levels: No threes: you learn in practice, through experience rather than from books.
One 3: curiosity about the world that needs a concrete goal.
Two 3s: a gift for the exact sciences, order and analysis.
Three: the strong mind of a researcher; learning new things comes easily to you.
Four or more: a scientist's mind, sometimes too deep in analysis. It helps to come back to the concrete.

4.title: Health
levels: No fours: the tradition speaks of a need to take particular care of your fitness, with movement and a daily rhythm.
One 4: average stamina that good habits can easily strengthen.
Two 4s: good fitness and resilience.
Three: great physical stamina, often a love of sport.
Four or more: great physical stamina; take care not to overload your body.

5.title: Intuition
levels: No fives: decisions are better made after thought and with a plan.
One 5: intuition works, but doubts sometimes drown it out.
Two 5s: good intuition combined with logic; you judge situations accurately.
Three: strong hunches; they are worth trusting, but check the facts.
Four or more: remarkable intuition. Trust it, but do not give up on the facts.

6.title: Work
levels: No sixes: you feel better doing mental work than physical work.
One 6: physical work tends to be a necessity rather than a pleasure.
Two 6s: skilful hands, a talent for craft and practical things.
Three: a need to make something tangible; work gives you balance.
Four or more: a strong need for physical work and making things; you find it hard to sit idle.

7.title: Talent
levels: No sevens: success comes from perseverance, not from chance.
One 7: a hidden talent worth discovering.
Two 7s: a clear talent and “luck” in what you do.
Three: many talents; what matters is choosing one and developing it.
Four or more: many talents, but also a tendency to scatter your efforts. Choose one path.

8.title: Duty
levels: No eights: a relaxed approach to obligations; clear rules help.
One 8: responsibility comes with age and experience.
Two 8s: a strong sense of duty and care for others.
Three: great responsibility. Remember not to carry everything alone.
Four or more: a very strong sense of duty. Remember that you do not have to rescue everyone.

9.title: Memory
levels: No nines: you remember better by doing than by listening.
One 9: a good memory that practice develops.
Two 9s: a sharp mind and a good memory.
Three: an exceptional memory and quick thinking.
Four or more: an outstanding memory and sharpness; it is worth giving your mind a rest.

1.title: Pinnacle of independence
1.text: A stage of standing on your own feet: decisions, initiative, the courage to go your own way. How to use it: make your own decisions and start new things, even when you are not sure.

2.title: Pinnacle of cooperation
2.text: A stage of relationships and partnership: patience, diplomacy, building bridges between people. How to use it: invest in relationships, listen and learn to work with others. Success will come through people.

3.title: Pinnacle of expression
3.text: A stage of creativity, contacts and joy; a good time to show the world what you have to say. How to use it: create, write, perform, meet people. Your expression opens doors.

4.title: Pinnacle of building
4.text: A stage of groundwork: stability, home, finances, steady effort that pays off. How to use it: build solid foundations, such as education, savings and a home. Patience pays off.

5.title: Pinnacle of change
5.text: A stage of movement, travel and new experiences: plenty of change, little boredom. How to use it: travel, learn, change things, but choose changes that make sense.

6.title: Pinnacle of care
6.text: A stage of family, home and responsibility for others; important relationships and commitments. How to use it: look after your home and loved ones, but do not forget your own needs.

7.title: Pinnacle of seeking
7.text: A stage of reflection, learning and going deeper into yourself, with more questions about meaning than about comfort. How to use it: give yourself time for study, reflection and spirituality. The answers will come from within.

8.title: Pinnacle of agency
8.text: A stage of career, influence and money; a time for ambitious goals and mature handling of resources. How to use it: set ambitious goals and manage your resources wisely. This is a time of influence.

9.title: Pinnacle of completion
9.text: A stage of the wide view, of sharing experience and closing old chapters. How to use it: share your experience, help others and close what has run its course.

0.title: Challenge of choice
0.text: There is no single theme; the challenge is choosing what you want to learn. All roads are open. Tip: listen to your intuition when choosing. No one path is imposed on you.

1.title: Challenge of independence
1.text: Learning to express yourself and set boundaries, without giving in and without digging in. Tip: practise saying “I want” and “I don't want”, calmly but firmly.

2.title: Challenge of sensitivity
2.text: Learning not to take everything personally and not to give yourself up for the sake of peace and quiet. Tip: do not take on other people's moods; your needs count too.

3.title: Challenge of expression
3.text: Learning to talk about feelings and to show your creative work in spite of criticism. Tip: share what you make before it is perfect.

4.title: Challenge of order
4.text: Learning discipline and patience, without rigidity and without chaos. Tip: small, regular steps instead of bursts of effort and chaos.

5.title: Challenge of freedom
5.text: Learning to use freedom wisely, without running away and without dropping everything at once. Tip: before you escape into something new, check what you are escaping from.

6.title: Challenge of responsibility
6.text: Learning to care for others without controlling them and without forgetting yourself. Tip: help, but do not rescue people against their will, and do not control.

7.title: Challenge of trust
7.text: Learning openness and trust in yourself, in others and in life. Tip: trust someone enough to tell them what you really think.

8.title: Challenge of power and money
8.text: Learning a healthy approach to money, ambition and control. Tip: money and power are tools. Ask what they are meant to serve.

13.title: Karmic debt 13
13.text: In the numerological tradition 13 stands for a lesson in work and perseverance: easy shortcuts rarely work, while patient effort brings lasting results.

14.title: Karmic debt 14
14.text: 14 is a lesson in moderation and freedom: learning to enjoy liberty without excess and without running from commitments.

16.title: Karmic debt 16
16.text: 16 is a lesson in humility and rebuilding: sometimes something has to fall apart so that something truer can take its place.

19.title: Karmic debt 19
19.text: 19 is a lesson in self-reliance that does not rule out asking for help: strength grows when you let others support you.
